business_problem: BlackRock needed a higher-scale repository for nightly file ingestion, derived risk analytics, and client-ready data products than its previous warehouse architecture could support.
solution_summary: BlackRock made Snowflake a core layer in its Aladdin data architecture so first-party data, third-party feeds, and calculation-derived analytics can be landed once and reused across investment workflows. Millions of files from index providers, security-reference vendors, and other sources flow through BlackRock's enterprise data platform into Snowflake, where they become the central repository for ingestion, storage, organization, and distribution. The same foundation stores large time-series outputs from BlackRock's risk analytics engines and serves that data to internal Aladdin environments, dashboards, applications, and Aladdin Data Cloud. Because Snowflake scales across clouds and regions, clients get a database-ready data-as-a-service experience instead of raw files and self-managed infrastructure. Secure sharing and standardized pipeline methods also speed onboarding of external providers and reduce data movement, turning Aladdin into a governed whole-portfolio data platform.

data_flow: Nightly files from index providers, security-reference vendors, ABOR and IBOR systems, and other sources are landed once into Snowflake via BlackRock's enterprise data platform. Derived analytics and time-series risk results remain in Snowflake, then flow into Aladdin environments and Aladdin Data Cloud for reports, dashboards, applications, and managed client delivery.
business_outcome: BlackRock now processes more than 116 billion data points and serves over 1.5 million on-demand reports through Aladdin while onboarding data faster and lowering overhead for both internal teams and clients.
